questions.question: A wide tibble holds emissions with one row per country and year and one column per sector (`Transport`, `Buildings`, `Waste`). For the question "total emissions per sector", which shape is tidy?
options: The wide table: each country-year is one row with all its sectors.
Neither: a tidy table may have only a single numeric column.
The long table: here an observation is one country-year-sector.
Both equally: tidiness never depends on the question asked.

questions.question: A wide tibble has the columns `Country`, `Year`, `Transport`, `Buildings` and `Waste`. In `wide %>% pivot_longer(cols = Transport:Waste, names_to = "Sector", values_to = "Emissions")`, what does the new column `Sector` contain?
options: the old column names `"Transport"`, `"Buildings"` and `"Waste"`
the numbers that stood in the columns `Transport` to `Waste`
one value per original row: the name of its largest sector
the names of the columns that were not stacked, such as `Country`

questions.question: A long tibble has the columns `Country`, `Year`, `Sector` and `Emissions`. In `pivot_wider(names_from = Sector, values_from = Emissions)`, what decides the rows of the result?
options: the distinct values of `Sector`, one row for each sector
the original rows of the long table, which are all kept
the column `Emissions`, one row per distinct emission value
the distinct combinations of `Country` and `Year`

questions.question: A wide tibble with 6 rows and 3 value columns, holding no missing values, is turned into a long tibble with `pivot_longer()`. Which statement about the long tibble is correct?
options: It holds fewer numbers, as repeated values are stored once.
Each of the 18 numbers appears in it exactly once.
Each number appears three times, once per stacked column.
It holds the 6 row totals instead of the separate values.

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached and `w <- tibble(id = c(1, 2, 3, 4), a = c(1, 2, 3, 4), b = c(5, 6, 7, 8), c = c(9, 10, 11, 12))`, what does `nrow(pivot_longer(w, cols = a:c, names_to = "k", values_to = "v"))` return?

With the tidyverse attached and `l <- tibble(country = c("A", "A", "B", "B", "C", "C"), year = c(2020, 2021, 2020, 2021, 2020, 2021), v = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6))`, what does `dim(pivot_wider(l, names_from = year, values_from = v))` return?
With the tidyverse attached and `w <- tibble(id = c(1, 2), a = c(1, 2), b = c(3, 4))`, what does `w %>% pivot_longer(cols = a:b, names_to = "key", values_to = "val") %>% pull(val)` return?
With the tidyverse attached and `w <- tibble(name = c("p", "q"), x = c(1, 2), y = c(3, 4))`, what does `names(pivot_longer(w, cols = x:y, names_to = "var", values_to = "num"))` return?
options: `[1] "var" "num"`
`[1] "name" "var"  "num"`
`[1] "name" "x"    "y"    "var"  "num"`
`[1] "name" "num"  "var"`

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached and `l <- tibble(id = c(1, 1, 2, 2), k = c("a", "b", "a", "b"), v = c(5, 6, 7, 8))`, what does `l %>% pivot_wider(names_from = k, values_from = v) %>% pull(a)` return?
With the tidyverse attached and `w <- tibble(id = c(1, 2, 3), a = c(4, NA, 6), b = c(7, 8, 9))`, what does `nrow(pivot_longer(w, cols = a:b, names_to = "k", values_to = "v"))` return?

`wide` has one row per `Country` and `Year` and the sector columns `Transport`, `Buildings` and `Waste`. After `long <- wide %>% pivot_longer(cols = Transport:Waste, names_to = "Sector", values_to = "Emissions")`, which columns together identify a single row of `long`?
options: `Country` and `Year`, as in the wide table
`Country`, `Year` and the new column `Sector`
`Sector` alone, the column the pivot created
`Emissions` alone, as each value appears once

questions.question: Spreading a column `Year` with the values 2020 and 2021 by `pivot_wider(names_from = Year, values_from = Total)` creates columns named `2020` and `2021`. Why is the argument `names_prefix = "Year_"` useful here?
options: Without a prefix, `pivot_wider()` renumbers the years as 1 and 2.
Without a prefix, the new columns overwrite the original column `Year`.
The prefix makes `pivot_wider()` sort the new columns by year.
A name starting with a digit needs backticks; `Year_2020` does not.

questions.question: A tibble has the columns `Country`, `Year`, `Transport`, `Buildings` and `Waste`, in that order. Which `cols` argument of `pivot_longer()` does not stack all three sector columns?
options: `cols = Transport:Waste`
`cols = 3:5`
`cols = c(Transport, Buildings, Waste)`
`cols = Transport:Buildings`

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached and `w <- tibble(id = c(1, 2), a = c(1, 2), b = c(3, 5))`, what does `w %>% pivot_longer(a:b, names_to = "k", values_to = "v") %>% group_by(k) %>% summarise(t = sum(v)) %>% pull(t)` return?
With the tidyverse attached and `l <- tibble(id = c(1, 1, 2), k = c("a", "b", "a"), v = c(5, 6, 7))`, what does `l %>% pivot_wider(names_from = k, values_from = v) %>% pull(b)` return?
options: an error, as the combination of `id` 2 and `"b"` is missing

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached and `w <- tibble(id = c(1, 2), a = c(1, 2), b = c(3, 4), c = c(5, 6))`, what does `w %>% pivot_longer(cols = c(a, c), names_to = "k", values_to = "v") %>% pull(b)` return?
options: an error, because `b` lies between the stacked columns

questions.question: For a long tibble with identifying columns and the columns `k` and `v`, when does `pivot_wider(names_from = k, values_from = v)` warn that the output will contain list-columns?
options: When a combination of the identifying columns and `k` occurs in more than one row.
When some combination of the identifying columns and `k` does not occur at all.
When `v` contains missing values that cannot be placed in a cell.
When `k` has more distinct values than the table has rows.

questions.question: A table has one row per country, year and sector, with the column `Emissions`. An analyst needs, for each country and year, the ratio of transport to building emissions. Which shape suits this question?
options: Long, as it is: tidy tables are always long, so the ratio is computed there.
Either: long and wide tables answer the same questions equally easily.
Long, grouped by sector, since the ratio is a summary over sectors.
Wide, one row per country-year, so the ratio is a `mutate()` of two columns.

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached and `l <- tibble(id = c(1, 1, 2, 2), yr = c(1, 2, 1, 2), v = c(5, 6, 7, 8), note = c("p", "q", "r", "s"))`, what does `nrow(pivot_wider(l, names_from = yr, values_from = v))` return?
options: an error, because `note` is not named in the pivot

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, `l <- tibble(id = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3), k = c("a", "b", "a", "b", "a"), v = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5))` has 5 rows. What does `l %>% pivot_wider(names_from = k, values_from = v) %>% pivot_longer(cols = a:b, names_to = "k", values_to = "v") %>% nrow()` return?
